overall: July 9 minutes were found insufficiently detailed but the Board cured this by amending them; motion-name and vote-recording claims were rejected; the July 19 minutes and notice claims were untimely and declined. No further relief ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the July 9, 2013 minutes lacked sufficient detail, as they referred to a recording for the discussion of proposed regulations.
allegations.key_passage: We find that although the Board timely provided the July 9, 2013 minutes in response to Mr. Logan's request, the minutes were not sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the amended minutes still omitted the names of members who made and seconded motions.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require public bodies to include in the minutes the names of specific public body members who make and second motions.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the amended minutes failed to record numerous votes taken at the July 9, 2013 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find this to be sufficient to meet the Open Meeting Law's requirements that minutes include "decisions made and the actions taken at each meeting, including the record of all votes."

allegations.summary: Complainant said the Board failed to provide July 19, 2013 minutes after a July 27 request; the complaint was filed late.
allegations.key_passage: Because Mr. Logan filed his complaint on September 16, 2013—39 days after the alleged violation—we find the allegation to be untimely and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to post notice of its July 19, 2013 meeting; the complaint was filed 59 days later.
allegations.key_passage: Because the alleged violation was reasonably discoverable at the time this meeting occurred, we find this allegation is untimely and decline to review it.
